title: Germiyanids
capsule: The Germiyanids were a Turkoman dynasty that controlled the Kütahya region of western Anatolia from around 1300, emerging as one of the many Anatolian beyliks (principalities) that arose as Mongol power receded and the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum fragmented. At their zenith in the early 14th century they were among the most powerful beyliks, with Germiyan Bey controlling territory stretching toward Denizli and Afyon. The dynasty was progressively subordinated to Ottoman expansion: Kütahya was ceded to the Ottomans by dowry in 1381, temporarily restored after the Battle of Ankara (1402), and permanently reincorporated into the Ottoman state in 1429 under Murad II.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Germiyanid territorial extent is approximately known from Ottoman, Byzantine, and Mamluk sources and from numismatic evidence, but precise borders between the beyliks are uncertain and contested in the scholarly literature.
